answer:
The last two digits are found modulo \(100\).

### 1. Last two digits of \(7^{2026}\)

Since
\[
7^4=2401\equiv 1 \pmod{100},
\]
the powers of \(7\) modulo \(100\) repeat every \(4\). Now
\[
2026\equiv 2 \pmod 4,
\]
so
\[
7^{2026}\equiv 7^2=49 \pmod{100}.
\]
Thus the last two digits are
\[
\boxed{49}.
\]

**Check by CRT:**  
Modulo \(4\):
\[
7^{2026}\equiv (-1)^{2026}\equiv 1 \pmod 4.
\]
Modulo \(25\): since \(\varphi(25)=20\),
\[
2026\equiv 6 \pmod{20}.
\]
Also \(7^2=49\equiv -1\pmod{25}\), so
\[
7^6\equiv (7^2)^3\equiv (-1)^3\equiv -1\equiv 24\pmod{25}.
\]
We need \(x\equiv 1\pmod 4\) and \(x\equiv 24\pmod{25}\). The solution is
\[
x\equiv 49\pmod{100}.
\]
So the last two digits are again \(\boxed{49}\).

---

### 2. Last two digits of \(3^{2026}\)

We have
\[
3^{10}\equiv 49 \pmod{100},
\]
so
\[
3^{20}\equiv 49^2=2401\equiv 1\pmod{100}.
\]
Thus powers of \(3\) modulo \(100\) repeat every \(20\). Since
\[
2026\equiv 6\pmod{20},
\]
we get
\[
3^{2026}\equiv 3^6=729\equiv 29\pmod{100}.
\]
Thus the last two digits are
\[
\boxed{29}.
\]

**Check by CRT:**  
Modulo \(4\):
\[
3^{2026}\equiv (-1)^{2026}\equiv 1\pmod 4.
\]
Modulo \(25\):
\[
2026\equiv 6\pmod{20},
\]
and
\[
3^6=729\equiv 4\pmod{25}.
\]
So we need \(x\equiv 1\pmod 4\) and \(x\equiv 4\pmod{25}\). Numbers congruent to \(4\pmod{25}\) are
\[
4,29,54,79,\dots
\]
Among these, \(29\equiv 1\pmod 4\). Therefore
\[
x\equiv 29\pmod{100}.
\]
So the last two digits are again \(\boxed{29}\).

\[
\boxed{7^{2026}\equiv 49\pmod{100},\qquad 3^{2026}\equiv 29\pmod{100}.}
\]

Final answers:  
\[
\boxed{49 \text{ and } 29}
\]
